title: Recipient verification passport
problem_or_outcome: Recipient eligibility, identity and sanctions status known at grant time
proposed_alternative: One continuously refreshed, versioned evidence record per recipient (EIN, Pub 78/BMF class, revocation, OFAC, bank verification, determinations) reused by every grant
mechanism: Verification is a property of the recipient not the transaction; refresh on source change, not on request
assumptions: Recipients recur within a sponsor; refresh cadence of IRS/OFAC sources is known
evidence_supporting: Fidelity ~12.5 grants per recipient (FINAL-STATUS PR #73); top-1,000 recipients receive ~49-54% of top-50 dollars (recipient-concentration data)
legal_constraints: Rev. Proc. 2018-32 reliance on IRS data at grant time; OFAC is a strict-liability regime so list versions must be current
technical_dependencies: IRS bulk files; OFAC lists; payee verification provider
human_responsibilities: Grants compliance owns refresh policy and exceptions
expected_benefits: Per-grant verification work collapses to per-recipient refresh; dated evidence for every grant
failure_modes: Stale record used after a status change; record poisoning via bad source load
cost_implications: Lower variable cost; fixed refresh cost
competitive_implications: Incumbents can build it; advantage is execution plus evidence trail
validation_method: Experiment E1 on synthetic grant streams; reuse measured on Schedule I data

title: Cross-sponsor verification network
problem_or_outcome: Same as INN-01 across sponsors
proposed_alternative: Shared evidence ledger with provenance; each sponsor still decides under its own policy; contributors earn credits
mechanism: If recipients recur across sponsors, the k-th sponsor finds most of its recipients already verified
assumptions: Recipients overlap across sponsors; sponsors accept shared evidence; liability stays with each sponsor
evidence_supporting: Pending: Schedule I cross-sponsor overlap harvest (08-experiments/recipient-overlap-evidence.md)
legal_constraints: Each sponsor retains decision; shared due-diligence reliance must be evaluated by counsel (API-12 issue); privacy of donor data excluded from network
technical_dependencies: Neutral operator; data-sharing agreements; evidence schemas
human_responsibilities: Each sponsor's compliance officer accepts or overrides
expected_benefits: Large reduction in duplicated verification; better coverage of small recipients
failure_modes: Free riding; a poisoned record propagates; antitrust/data rules; cold start
cost_implications: Network operator fixed cost; marginal cost falls with members
adoption_barriers: High: competitors sharing; trust; legal opinion
competitive_implications: If mechanism real, network effects favor first credible neutral operator; Candid and Chariot are partial incumbents
validation_method: Overlap curve from public data (E7); legal analysis

title: Pre-verified recipient universe (begin before the request)
problem_or_outcome: Routine grants decided instantly
existing_approach: Verification starts when a recommendation arrives
proposed_alternative: Continuously maintain verified status for the universe of likely recipients (all 501(c)(3) public charities on Pub 78 plus every past payee) so recommendation-time work is a lookup
mechanism: Moves verification off the critical path entirely
assumptions: Bulk data covers most recipients; long tail resolvable on demand
evidence_supporting: IRS publishes full Pub 78/BMF/revocation files (industry report §2.6)
failure_modes: Name ambiguity at request time; churches absent from 990 data (8.3% of top-50 dollars to church-status recipients without e-filed 990)

title: Reusable non-routine determinations
method: A first principles + D insurance underwriting
problem_or_outcome: Foreign, fiscal-sponsor and ER grants handled lawfully
proposed_alternative: Versioned determination artifacts (equivalency determination, fiscal-sponsor review, ER pre-qualification) with expiry and scope, reused across grants and accounts
mechanism: Legal judgment attaches to the organization and arrangement, not the individual grant
assumptions: Determinations remain valid for a period; reuse is legally acceptable within the same sponsor
evidence_supporting: Exceptions cluster by recipient (12.5 grants/recipient at Fidelity); foreign 1.46% of dollars; core proxy 7.76% of lines
legal_constraints: ED/ER rules; reliance on another party's ED requires counsel (Notice 2006-109 unverified, regulatory map)
human_responsibilities: Specialist makes and renews each determination
expected_benefits: Specialist minutes per grant fall with reuse factor
cost_implications: Large saving if reuse factor high
validation_method: Measure reuse factor on partner history; E2

title: Risk-tiered policy-as-code approval
problem_or_outcome: Routine grants approved fast; risky ones reviewed
existing_approach: Manual queue for many or all grants
proposed_alternative: Deterministic policy approves routine tier; flags route exceptions; AI flags only
mechanism: Statutory exposure is narrow for listed public charities
assumptions: Board approves thresholds; rules back-tested
evidence_supporting: Parent PoC: 59 tests incl. routine approval, referral, holds
human_responsibilities: Policy owners approve versions; specialists decide exceptions
expected_benefits: Removes per-grant human touch for the routine tier
failure_modes: Misconfigured rule at scale; regulator reads as weak control
validation_method: Parent PoC; E2 approval architecture simulation

title: Acceptance sampling instead of per-item review (routine tier)
problem_or_outcome: Assurance that routine approvals are correct
proposed_alternative: Zero per-item review in the routine tier plus continuous statistical acceptance sampling with seeded defects; sampling rate adapts to defect findings
mechanism: Per-item review cost scales with volume; sampling cost scales with risk; seeded defects measure detection
assumptions: Defect rate in routine tier is very low; sampling detects drift
evidence_supporting: Revoked-EIN grants 0.082% of top-50 dollars (strategic synthesis §0)
legal_constraints: Sponsor must still be able to show control; sampling design documented
expected_benefits: Human effort proportional to risk not volume
failure_modes: Rare catastrophic defects slip between samples; complacency

title: Verified payee registry (recipient-enrolled)
problem_or_outcome: Funds reach the right recipient account
existing_approach: Each sponsor collects and verifies bank details; checks
proposed_alternative: Recipients enroll once (verified bank account, contacts, preferences); sponsors pay only to registry endpoints; changes go through cooling-off and out-of-band verification
mechanism: Payee verification is per recipient, shared across sponsors and grants
assumptions: Recipients will enroll; registry operator trusted
evidence_supporting: Fragmented rails (four camps); processors' complaints about payout rules; DAFpay network exists (EV-053)
legal_constraints: No law requires checks; NACHA rules; money transmission if registry holds funds (it must not)
expected_benefits: Fewer checks; fewer hijacks; lower recipient cost
competitive_implications: Network effect via two-sided enrollment (needs proof)

title: Structured remittance with grant ID
problem_or_outcome: Recipient can attribute and thank
proposed_alternative: Grant ID plus donor-choice data in CCD+/CTX addenda or ISO 20022 remittance, retrievable by recipient API
mechanism: Reconciliation needs a shared key carried with the money
assumptions: Recipient banks pass addenda; nonprofits' systems can read them
evidence_supporting: No readable top-10 sponsor states a grant ID in addenda (EV-086)

title: Daily netting of grants per recipient
problem_or_outcome: Lower payment cost and recipient reconciliation
proposed_alternative: Aggregate all approved grants to one recipient per day into one payment with itemized remittance
mechanism: Payment cost and reconciliation scale with payments not grants
assumptions: Recipients receive many grants (12.5/recipient at Fidelity annually); legal grant identity preserved in remittance
evidence_supporting: Grant concentration data
legal_constraints: Each grant remains a separately decided distribution; acknowledgment per grant
failure_modes: One payment failure delays many grants; a return affects multiple grants
validation_method: E3 payment count reduction on synthetic distribution calibrated to concentration

title: Recipient-pull claiming
problem_or_outcome: Funds reach recipient
proposed_alternative: Approved grants appear in a verified recipient inbox; recipient claims to its registered account; unclaimed grants escalate
mechanism: Recipient authentication replaces sponsor-side payee maintenance
assumptions: Recipients will log in; unclaimed handled
evidence_supporting: Processor complaints about lost checks (gap19)
legal_constraints: Escheat rules for unclaimed; grant completion timing
expected_benefits: No checks; recipient controls account details

title: Pre-underwritten asset acceptance
problem_or_outcome: Complex asset accepted or declined prudently
proposed_alternative: Asset-class underwriting rules give instant indicative acceptance and a standard document set; specialists handle only rule exceptions
mechanism: Most complexity is repeated within asset classes
assumptions: Asset classes are standardizable (public restricted stock, LP interests on known platforms, real estate types)
evidence_supporting: Non-cash vendors exist with standardized intake (b40n14-03)
human_responsibilities: Specialist decides exceptions and final acceptance above threshold
expected_benefits: Faster indicative answers; less specialist time

title: Liquidation partner pre-commitment
problem_or_outcome: Illiquid assets converted prudently
proposed_alternative: Pre-negotiated partners (secondary markets, real-estate buyers) bid on accepted asset classes under standing agreements
mechanism: Price discovery and speed via standing liquidity providers
assumptions: Partners exist for major classes
evidence_supporting: Non-cash vendor market (b40n14-03)

title: Structured legal-document exchange for gifts
problem_or_outcome: Gift documents complete and correct
proposed_alternative: Machine-readable gift packet (assignment, appraisal summary, 8283 data) exchanged with advisors and attorneys via API
mechanism: Re-keying and missing-document loops come from unstructured exchange
assumptions: Counterparties adopt formats
evidence_supporting: None specific

title: Zero-ticket servicing
problem_or_outcome: Donor knows status and can act
proposed_alternative: Shared state projections plus proactive event notifications plus grounded answers; humans only for recovery and exceptions
mechanism: Most contacts are status questions caused by hidden state
assumptions: Status share of contacts is high
evidence_supporting: No published response-time promises; complaints about timing (EV)
failure_modes: Hallucinated answers; donors who prefer people

title: Invisible, advisor-embedded DAF
problem_or_outcome: Donors reached at low cost; advisors keep relationship
proposed_alternative: DAF capabilities embedded in advisor and wealth platforms via APIs; sponsor brand recedes
mechanism: Distribution is channel-led; advisors control the client relationship
assumptions: Advisors want embedded tools; platforms will integrate
evidence_supporting: RCF-Ren spine across ~11 wealth programs; channel-led growth [I]
legal_constraints: Proposed 4966 regs would make managing advisers donor-advisors (proposed only); fee disclosure

title: Scoped delegation tokens
problem_or_outcome: Advisors and agents act within authority
existing_approach: Paper LOAs; credential sharing (banned by terms)
proposed_alternative: OAuth-style scoped, revocable, capped delegations per advisor or agent
mechanism: Authorization is data, not documents
assumptions: Partners can integrate OAuth
evidence_supporting: Six of top 20 restrict automated access (EV-122); agentic products lack limits (EV-088)
human_responsibilities: Donor grants; staff only on exceptions

title: DAF transfer protocol (ACATS-like)
problem_or_outcome: Donor can move to another sponsor with history
proposed_alternative: Standard sponsor-to-sponsor transfer message: eligibility check, optional in-kind securities, open grant record history, agreed timelines
mechanism: Standardized messaging made brokerage transfers routine
assumptions: Receiving and sending sponsors adopt; in-kind permitted
evidence_supporting: No published outbound policy; 10 days-4 weeks (EV-121); $8.03bn DAF-to-DAF netted FY2024
legal_constraints: Transfer is a grant to an eligible sponsor; sending sponsor decides
validation_method: Prototype with open grant record; E8

title: Always-migrated record (event-log replay)
problem_or_outcome: History survives platform change
proposed_alternative: Continuous full-fidelity export of the event log; migration = replay into the new system
mechanism: Migration loss comes from schema conversion at a single point
assumptions: Target systems can ingest events
evidence_supporting: AEF kept 2 years (EV-037)
expected_benefits: No history loss; lower switching cost

title: Spend-down horizons and goal-based standing instructions
problem_or_outcome: Dormant capital reaches charity
proposed_alternative: Donor chooses an optional granting horizon or recurring plan at opening; system schedules grants; inactivity triggers charitable defaults under policy
mechanism: Defaults strongly shape behavior; idle accounts lack a plan
assumptions: Donors accept optional horizons
evidence_supporting: 22% of accounts no grants 2020-22; median 3-yr payout 9% (EV-015)
legal_constraints: No federal payout mandate (EV-093); donor advisory privileges must be respected
cost_implications: Lower revenue under asset fees (incentive conflict)

title: Continuous compliance evidence ledger and auto audit package
problem_or_outcome: Auditors and regulators obtain evidence efficiently
proposed_alternative: Every control emits evidence when it operates; audit package generated on demand; auditor read access
mechanism: Evidence produced by operation costs nothing extra
assumptions: Auditors accept system evidence
evidence_supporting: No sponsor publishes operating metrics (EV-076)
validation_method: Parent PoC evidence records; coverage test

title: Policy compiler with back-testing
problem_or_outcome: Policy reflects law and is applied consistently
proposed_alternative: Human-authored policy compiled to decision tables plus tests plus generated prose; back-test against history before publish
mechanism: Compilers turn specifications into verified executables with tests
assumptions: Policies expressible as rules
evidence_supporting: Strategic synthesis §B structural change 1

title: Continuous close
problem_or_outcome: Books correct and agree with custodian and bank
proposed_alternative: Reconciliation as continuously evaluated invariants; month-end is a checkpoint plus controller attestation (CTL-048)
mechanism: Breaks are detected when they occur, so aging is short
assumptions: Custodian and bank feeds available daily
evidence_supporting: GAP-005 (no data)

title: Per-donor contribution references (virtual account numbers)
problem_or_outcome: Contributions attributed automatically
proposed_alternative: Each intent gets a unique reference or virtual account / sub-account at the custodian; matching becomes deterministic
mechanism: Unique keys eliminate matching
assumptions: Custodian supports references or sub-accounts
evidence_supporting: None public

title: Reliance on upstream verified identity (custodian or advisor KYC attestations)
problem_or_outcome: Donor identity known without repeat verification
proposed_alternative: Accept signed identity attestations from the advisor's custodian or a verified identity wallet, with risk-based step-up
mechanism: Identity already verified by regulated institutions upstream
assumptions: Attestations available and reliable; reliance acceptable as a risk control (not BSA-mandated)
evidence_supporting: Regulatory map: KYC is a risk control, not BSA mandate, for sponsors

title: Continuous onboarding (account at first intent)
problem_or_outcome: Account established lawfully
proposed_alternative: Account opens at first contribution intent with minimal data; further data collected only when a decision needs it
mechanism: Most fields are only needed for specific later decisions
assumptions: Agreement acceptance and identity at minimum assurance are enough to accept a gift
evidence_supporting: None
legal_constraints: Agreement acceptance needed before advisory privileges; acknowledgment content
failure_modes: Incomplete data at grant time; successor gaps

title: Donor agents as delegated principals with caps
problem_or_outcome: Donor-side AI acts safely
existing_approach: Credential sharing or uncapped MCP tools
proposed_alternative: Scoped agent delegations; confirmation above cap by the delegating donor
mechanism: Authority is bounded by data the sponsor enforces
assumptions: Donors use agents
evidence_supporting: EV-088/089: agentic products lack limits

title: Pipeline-based liquidity planning with seasonal buffer
problem_or_outcome: Liquidity covers outflows including stress
proposed_alternative: Forecast outflows from the recommendation pipeline, scheduled grants and seasonality; buffer set to days of peak outflow
mechanism: Grant intents are an order book
assumptions: Pipeline predictive
evidence_supporting: Twin: 30-day custodian outage in surge exhausts 2% buffer

title: Shared specialist pool across sponsors
problem_or_outcome: Non-routine cases decided by competent specialists
proposed_alternative: A shared pool of grants-compliance and complex-asset specialists serving multiple sponsors under each sponsor's delegated authority
mechanism: Specialist demand is lumpy; pooling smooths utilization
assumptions: Sponsors delegate case work while keeping decision
evidence_supporting: Twin: surge breaches and single-specialist concentration
legal_constraints: Decision authority stays with each sponsor; conflicts
human_responsibilities: Specialists act under each sponsor's delegation

title: Recipient attestation at claim (two-sided benefit evidence)
problem_or_outcome: Prohibited benefit absent
existing_approach: Donor certification; staff review of purpose text
proposed_alternative: Recipient attests no goods or services provided and no pledge satisfaction, at enrollment and per flagged grant
mechanism: The recipient knows whether benefits were provided
assumptions: Recipients answer truthfully; attestation adds evidence not liability transfer
evidence_supporting: None specific
legal_constraints: 4967 liability stays with donor/manager; attestation is evidence only

title: Digital twin as management system
problem_or_outcome: Staffing and change decisions grounded in evidence
proposed_alternative: Measured twin drives staffing, surge and change decisions; simulated vs measured labeled
mechanism: Queue theory predicts SLA breaches before they occur
assumptions: Telemetry available
evidence_supporting: Parent twin results

title: Outcome teams with agent owners, no departments
problem_or_outcome: Work flows without handoffs
proposed_alternative: Teams own outcomes; one exception queue; agent owners accountable for agent families
mechanism: Handoffs are created by departmental boundaries
assumptions: Specialists can work across outcomes
evidence_supporting: Parent org model

title: Continuous board assurance with expiring parameters
problem_or_outcome: Board oversight real and evidenced
proposed_alternative: Live evidence portal; every governed parameter has an owner and expiry; board approves deltas
mechanism: Oversight degrades when parameters drift unreviewed
assumptions: Board will use it
evidence_supporting: Clarity review FM-08

title: Evidence-graded, fairness-monitored recipient discovery
problem_or_outcome: Donors make informed choices without unsupported impact claims
proposed_alternative: Recipient information with evidence grades and disclosed ranking criteria; fairness monitoring by recipient segment
mechanism: Grades separate outputs from impact
assumptions: Grade rubric defensible
evidence_supporting: Church-status share 8.3% (strategic synthesis); ratings coverage gaps

title: Universe re-screening on list change (sanctions)
problem_or_outcome: Sanctions exposure cleared
proposed_alternative: Screen all parties, recipients and payees whenever a list changes; transactions check a pinned screening result
mechanism: List changes are rarer than transactions
assumptions: List versions available daily
evidence_supporting: OFAC record-keeping 10 years (regulatory map)
legal_constraints: OFAC strict liability; true matches decided by a person
failure_modes: Window between list publish and rescreen

title: Pay-first for pre-verified tier with post-payment assurance
problem_or_outcome: Fast routine grants
proposed_alternative: For recipients in the pre-verified set and small amounts, release payment immediately on request and assure by sampling afterwards
mechanism: Card networks accept small post-transaction risk for speed
assumptions: Ineligibility risk in tier is negligible; errors are recoverable
evidence_supporting: Revoked-EIN share 0.082% of dollars
legal_constraints: A taxable distribution cannot be undone by sampling; sponsor decision must precede payment
recommendation: Reject as stated; keep decide-then-pay with instant rule decision (INN-05)

title: Shared compliance policy packs
problem_or_outcome: Policies current with law across many sponsors
proposed_alternative: Central policy library (versioned, cited, back-tested) that sponsors adopt and parameterize; each board approves
mechanism: Law is common; parameters differ
assumptions: Sponsors accept a standard base
evidence_supporting: None

title: Year-end surge smoothing via flexible execution windows
problem_or_outcome: Year-end grants processed within SLA
proposed_alternative: Donors schedule year-end grants with an execution window; system levels specialist load; pre-clear known recipients in November
mechanism: Load leveling reduces peak capacity needs
assumptions: Donors accept windows where deductibility is unaffected
evidence_supporting: Twin: 34 days over SLA at surge
legal_constraints: Completed-gift date rules apply to contributions, not grants; grant timing has no donor tax effect

title: One recipient inbox API for all sponsors
problem_or_outcome: Recipient sees all incoming DAF grants in one place
proposed_alternative: Neutral recipient API aggregating grant notices, remittance and attribution across sponsors
mechanism: Recipient reconciliation cost is per sponsor relationship
assumptions: Sponsors publish grant events
evidence_supporting: Weak nonprofit leverage (industry report §3)
